chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
It is not proper for a Muslim woman to wear, from among khimārs and garments, that which does not cover anything.

key_terms.الدُّرُوعِ: garments or dresses worn as covering
key_terms.الْخُمُرِ: head-coverings or veils worn by women
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman; the legal subject addressed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمَةِ: the Muslim woman; specifying the believer bound by this ruling
key_terms.شَيْئًا: anything at all; indicating lack of sufficient covering

ai.seo_question: What kind of clothing is not suitable for a Muslim woman to wear in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning a Muslim woman's clothing, indicating that garments such as khimārs and dresses must provide actual covering. It is thematically connected to the conditions of valid dress in worship, especially salat (prayer), for a free woman.
